title: Machine code: reading 16-byte GB10 instructions and their scheduling bits
summary: A GB10 instruction is 128 bits in four little-endian words: opcode, predicate and registers in word 0, and a control word with stall (bits 9..12), yield, scoreboards and a wait mask. Drake learned the encoding from his own probe kernels with NVIDIA's tools as an offline oracle, Mesa's NAK, and the chip. I can decode the seed-built vector add with you: the add, IADD3 R9, PT, PT, R2, R5, RZ, waits on SB4, which both loads set.
goal: Read GB10 machine code field by field, including the scheduling bits a compiler normally hides.
key_steps: Split each 16-byte instruction into four little-endian words.
Read opcode, predicate and registers from word 0.
Read stall, yield, scoreboards and wait mask from word 3.
Name opcodes from a table you can check.
Compare against an independent expectation, not just the decoder.

example.code:
note Decode GB10 (sm_121) machine words: 16 bytes per instruction, four little-endian 32-bit
note words. Field positions from omega-mv seed/sm121/sm121.tbl (word 0: opcode in bits 0..11,
note predicate 12..15, destination 16..23, first source 24..31) and CUDApp's control-word note
note (word 3: stall 9..12, yield 13, write barrier 14..16, read barrier 17..19, wait mask 20..25).
note Input: exactly 512 bytes (32 instructions) on stdin. Exit 0 decoded, 3 wrong input length.
om2
global ob uchar 4096
global on ulong 1
global inb uchar 4096
global inn ulong 1
global inp ulong 1
text hx "0123456789abcdef"
fn putc c uchar to void
put ob get on 0 c
put on 0 add get on 0 1
end
fn puts s view uchar * to void
for i ulong len s
putc get s i
end
end
fn putdec v ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 21
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
while gt n 0 bound 21
n = sub n 1
putc get d n
end
end
fn puthex v ulong w ulong to void
putc 48
putc 120
for i ulong w
s = mul sub sub w 1 i 4
putc get hx and shr v s 0xf
end
end
fn flush to void
w = write 1 ob 0 get on 0
put on 0 0
end
note Read all of stdin; every pass adds at least one byte to a 4096-byte buffer.
fn slurp to bool
while lt get inn 0 4096 bound 4097
k = read 0 inb get inn 0 sub 4096 get inn 0
if lt k 0
ret false
end
if eq k 0
ret true
end
put inn 0 add get inn 0 ulong k
end
ret false
end
note Next decimal number in the input; returns 2^64-1 when none is left.
fn nextnum to ulong
v = ulong 0
seen = false
while lt get inp 0 get inn 0 bound 4097
c = get inb get inp 0
put inp 0 add get inp 0 1
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 ulong sub c 48
seen = true
else
if seen
ret v
end
end
end
if seen
ret v
end
ret 18446744073709551615
end
fn word i ulong k ulong to ulong
b = add mul i 16 mul k 4
lo = or ulong get inb b shl ulong get inb add b 1 8
hi = or shl ulong get inb add b 2 16 shl ulong get inb add b 3 24
ret or lo hi
end
text sop " op=0x"
text spr " pred="
text srd " rd="
text sra " ra="
text sst " | stall="
text syl " yield="
text swb " sets="
text srb " rsets="
text swt " waits="
text snone "-"
text ssb "SB"
text sia "IADD3 decoded: IADD3 "
text spt ", PT, PT, "
text scm ", "
fn hex3 v ulong to void
for i ulong 3
putc get hx and shr v mul sub 2 i 4 0xf
end
end
fn bar v ulong to void
if eq v 7
puts snone
else
puts ssb
putdec v
end
end
fn reg v ulong to void
if eq v 255
putc 82
putc 90
else
putc 82
putdec v
end
end
fn line i ulong to void
w0 = word i 0
w3 = word i 3
if lt i 10
putc 32
end
putdec i
puts sop
hex3 and w0 0xfff
puts spr
putdec and shr w0 12 0xf
puts srd
putdec and shr w0 16 0xff
puts sra
putdec shr w0 24
puts sst
putdec and shr w3 9 0xf
puts syl
putdec and shr w3 13 1
puts swb
bar and shr w3 14 7
puts srb
bar and shr w3 17 7
puts swt
m = and shr w3 20 0x3f
if eq m 0
puts snone
end
for b ulong 6
if eq and shr m b 1 1
puts ssb
putdec b
putc 32
end
end
putc 10
end
fn main to int
if not slurp
ret 3
end
if ne get inn 0 512
ret 3
end
for i ulong 32
line i
end
for i ulong 32
if eq and word i 0 0xfff 0x210
puts sia
reg and shr word i 0 16 0xff
puts spt
reg shr word i 0 24
puts scm
reg and word i 1 0xff
puts scm
reg and word i 2 0xff
putc 10
end
end
flush
ret 0
end

common_mistake: Treating the control word as optional or copying it between instructions. A wrong stall or wait does not fault; it gives wrong numbers. Decode every control word and keep golden words per instruction kind.

evidence_note: EXERCISED on a Linux AArch64 host: sass.om decodes omega-mv seed/sm121/vecadd.bin (sha256 39f3dfdf...); a one-bit mutant is caught by the comparison, not by the decoder. omega-mv records a historical chip run of these bytes on 2026-10-20 (run record dirty=3), not re-run here. CUDA++'s own disassembler (bar C6) is BUILDING.
